planting.note: Set rooted offshoots or tissue-cultured plantlets in deep, well-drained soil in full sun once spring temperatures are reliably warm.

directions: Khastawi is a soft, thin-skinned, amber-to-dark-brown date long favored as one of the leading fresh-eating cultivars of southern Iraq's Basra-area palm groves along the Shatt al-Arab. Because the fruit is harvested soft at the khalal/rutab stage rather than dried, growers often thin strands by roughly a third at pollination time to boost fruit size and sugar content. Give female trees a nearby male pollinator or hand-pollinate, and expect new offshoots to take four to five years before bearing a full crop. Long, hot, dry summers are essential to properly ripen and cure the fruit without spoilage.
sources: FAO Plant Production and Protection Paper 156: Date Palm Cultivation (Barreveld/Zaid)

planting.note: Set rooted offshoots in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, spacing widely for the mature crown.

directions: Sayer (also transliterated Sair) is one of Iraq's most widely planted commercial date cultivars, prized for its medium-sized amber-to-light-brown semi-dry fruit, which tolerates occasional humidity and rain near harvest better than fully soft varieties. It is grown extensively in the Tigris-Euphrates date groves of central and southern Iraq and is eaten fresh at the rutab stage or dried for storage and regional date-paste making. As with other dioecious date palms, fruit set depends on a male pollinator or hand pollination during the spring bloom.
sources: FAO Plant Production and Protection Paper 156: Date Palm Cultivation (Barreveld/Zaid)

planting.note: Set rooted offshoots in deep, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Dayri produces long, slender fruit that darkens to near-black with a chewy, semi-dry texture once fully cured on the bunch. Originating in Iraq's southern palm groves, it was later introduced to California's Coachella Valley, where growers sometimes know it by the anglicized name Derrie, prized there for weathering occasional harvest-season rain better than fully soft cultivars. Leave bunches on the tree to finish curing naturally rather than picking early, since the flavor concentrates as the fruit dries.
sources: FAO Plant Production and Protection Paper 156: Date Palm Cultivation (Barreveld/Zaid)

planting.note: Set rooted offshoots in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; expect slower offshoot increase than many other Iraqi cultivars.

directions: Mektoom (also spelled Maktoom) is a traditional soft-date cultivar from the Tigris-Euphrates palm groves of Iraq, harvested at the soft rutab stage for syrupy fresh eating rather than drying. It produces relatively few offshoots per trunk compared with heavy-suckering cultivars like Zahdi, so commercial nurseries propagate it more slowly, often relying more on tissue culture to build up planting stock. Give it the same long, hot growing season and dry harvest window that other Iraqi date cultivars require to cure properly.
sources: FAO Plant Production and Protection Paper 156: Date Palm Cultivation (Barreveld/Zaid)

planting.note: Set huli (corm-top cuttings) into rich, consistently moist upland beds once soil has warmed; does not require a flooded wetland patch.

directions: Tausala ni Samoa, whose name translates roughly as 'Lady of Samoa,' is a large white-cormed dalo (taro) cultivar of Samoan origin that became Fiji's dominant commercial taro variety after Samoa's own crop was devastated by taro leaf blight in the early 1990s, shifting much of the region's taro export trade to Fiji's volcanic hillside gardens. It is typically grown as a rain-fed upland crop rather than in flooded patches, favoring deep, fertile, well-draining soil and partial shade in hot lowland sites. Harvest corms roughly nine to twelve months after planting, and always cook the corms and leaves thoroughly before eating to break down calcium oxalate crystals.
sources: Secretariat of the Pacific Community (SPC) Land Resources Division taro variety reports
ACIAR reports on taro leaf blight and Pacific Island taro trade
